title: Basic Home Toolkit: The Tools That Handle Most Repairs
meta: The basic home toolkit for DIY repairs: the screwdrivers, pliers, testers, plungers and drywall tools that the most common home fixes actually call for, and what to look for.
summary: A drill/driver, a screwdriver set, adjustable wrench, tongue-and-groove pliers, a tape measure, a utility knife, a non-contact voltage tester, a flange plunger, putty knives, a level, a stepladder and a flashlight cover most of the repairs on this site. Buy those first and add specialty tools as jobs come up.

sections.title: Core hand tools
sections.intro: These show up in almost every guide.

items.name: Cordless drill/driver
items.why: Drives screws for drywall patches, hinges and strike plates, and drills pilot holes.
items.look_for: A compact 12V or 18/20V model with two batteries and an adjustable clutch so you do not strip screws.

items.name: Screwdriver set (Phillips and flat, several sizes)
items.why: Cover plates, handles, hinges and appliance panels.
items.look_for: Magnetic tips and comfortable handles. A multi-bit driver is a good space saver.

items.name: Adjustable wrench (8 and 10 inch)
items.why: Supply line nuts, toilet fill valves and faucet parts.
items.look_for: Smooth jaw adjustment with little play.

items.name: Tongue-and-groove pliers
items.why: Grip P-trap slip nuts, aerators and large fittings.
items.look_for: A 10 inch pair handles most household plumbing.

items.name: Needle-nose pliers
items.why: Small clips, wire loops and fishing out debris.
items.look_for: A built-in wire cutter.

items.name: Utility knife
items.why: Cutting old caulk, trimming drywall and screen mesh.
items.look_for: Retractable blade with easy blade changes. Keep spare blades.

items.name: Tape measure (25 foot)
items.why: Measuring for patches, flooring, screens and weatherstripping.
items.look_for: A wide, stiff blade that extends without bending.

items.name: Hex key (Allen) set
items.why: Faucet handle set screws and freeing a jammed garbage disposal (1/4 inch).
items.look_for: Both SAE and metric sizes.

sections.title: Safety and testing
sections.intro: Cheap tools that prevent expensive mistakes.

items.name: Non-contact voltage tester
items.why: Confirms power is off before you touch a switch, outlet or appliance wiring.
items.look_for: Audible and visual alerts. Test it on a known live outlet every time before use.

items.name: Plug-in outlet tester with GFCI button
items.why: Checks outlet wiring and trips GFCIs for testing.
items.look_for: A clear light code chart on the body.

items.name: Safety glasses, work gloves and dust masks
items.q: safety glasses work gloves dust mask kit
items.why: Scraping, sanding, grout removal and gutter work.
items.look_for: Glasses rated ANSI Z87.1 and masks sized for fine dust.

items.name: Flashlight or headlamp
items.why: Under sinks, inside walls, at the breaker panel.
items.look_for: A headlamp keeps both hands free.

sections.title: Plumbing basics
sections.intro: For the most common household emergencies.

items.name: Flange (toilet) plunger
items.why: Clears most toilet clogs.
items.look_for: A fold-out flange that seals the toilet drain opening.

items.name: Cup (sink) plunger
items.why: Sinks, tubs and showers.
items.look_for: A flat-bottom cup. Keep it separate from the toilet plunger.

items.name: Hand drain snake, 25 foot
items.why: Clogs past the P-trap.
items.look_for: A 1/4 inch cable with a lockable drum.

items.name: Closet (toilet) auger
items.why: Stubborn toilet clogs, without scratching porcelain.
items.look_for: A rubber sleeve at the bend.

items.name: Putty and taping knives (1 1/2, 6 and 10 inch)
items.why: Spreading and feathering joint compound.
items.look_for: Flexible stainless blades.

items.name: Dripless caulk gun
items.why: Tubs, sinks, trim and exterior gaps.
items.look_for: A smooth trigger and a pressure release so caulk does not keep oozing.

items.name: Sanding sponges
items.why: Smoothing patches with less dust than sandpaper.
items.look_for: Fine and medium grits.

items.name: Torpedo or 24 inch level
items.why: Hanging things straight and checking doors and frames.
items.look_for: Easy-to-read vials.

sections.title: Access
sections.intro: Most repairs need you a few feet off the floor.

items.name: Step ladder (4 to 6 foot)
items.why: Smoke alarms, light fixtures, high shelves.
items.look_for: A duty rating above your weight plus tools. Fiberglass for any electrical work.

items.name: Extension ladder with stabilizer
items.why: Gutters and one-story roof edges.
items.look_for: Right length to extend 3 feet past the gutter, and a standoff stabilizer.

faq.q: What tools should every homeowner have?
faq.a: A drill/driver, screwdrivers, adjustable wrench, pliers, utility knife, tape measure, voltage tester, plungers, putty knives, a stepladder and a flashlight cover the most common repairs.

faq.q: Should I buy a tool kit or individual tools?
faq.a: Pre-made kits are convenient but often include low-quality filler. Buying the core tools one at a time usually gets better quality where it matters.

faq.q: Do I need a voltage tester if I turn off the breaker?
faq.a: Yes. Breaker labels are often wrong and boxes can contain more than one circuit. Always verify at the device.
